title: Nuxt.js Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Nuxt.js course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: What does NuxtPage display?
options: The page matching the current route
Every page at the same time
exercises.explanation: NuxtPage is the place where Nuxt displays the page chosen by the address. It belongs in the app wrapper.

exercises.question: Which file makes the /books route?
exercises.explanation: A Vue file in pages becomes a route. index.vue is the home page, while books.vue makes /books.

exercises.question: Which prop gives NuxtLink its destination?
exercises.explanation: NuxtLink provides a normal link meaning while letting Nuxt handle local route navigation.

exercises.question: What does the layout slot hold?
exercises.explanation: A layout wraps pages with shared content. Its slot is the space for the selected page.

exercises.question: Where does this auto-imported component live?
exercises.explanation: Nuxt can auto-import components from its components folder. A component can receive props just like other Vue components.

exercises.question: What does useSeoMeta configure?
options: The number of rows in a database
Page metadata such as the title
exercises.explanation: useSeoMeta describes title and description values for a page. Nuxt can include them in the generated document head.

exercises.question: What is the purpose of the useState key?
options: To identify the shared state value
exercises.explanation: useState creates state that Nuxt can share safely within one app visit. A key identifies which state value is being requested.

exercises.question: Where should this public JSON file be stored?
exercises.explanation: useFetch can load data and give the page loading and error state. A file in public can act as simple build-time content.

exercises.question: What is slug in /books/moon-trip?
exercises.explanation: A bracketed page file captures part of an address. useRoute gives the page access to that route value.

exercises.question: Why read window inside onMounted?
options: window is available in the browser, not every rendering context
exercises.explanation: Some APIs exist only in the browser. onMounted runs after the component is mounted there, so it can safely read browser-only objects.

exercises.question: Can public runtime config safely hide a secret?
options: No, browser users can read it
Yes, its name keeps it hidden
exercises.explanation: Runtime config separates public settings from server-only settings. Anything placed in public is visible to browser code.

exercises.question: Which folder is served for this static result?
exercises.explanation: Nuxt can build a site as static files. List dynamic routes that cannot be found by following ordinary page links.
